title: Patch the W5-12 follow-up review findings before the next SIT deploy and proof round
fallback_model: Claude Sonnet only if the patch stays tightly scoped to the findings below
objective: Take the W5-12 implementation from 'feature mostly wired' to 'safe to redeploy' by fixing the two review findings Codex found in commit 3a87116: add proper company-access enforcement for the new live export path, and make reprocess/detail/export use the correct latest voucher state instead of stale earlier vouchers.
current_truth_from_codex_review: Commit 3a87116 is real and does wire W5-12 end to end in broad strokes: line-item storage, processing branch, review endpoints, and backend-built export rows are present.
However, the new live export path trusts any caller-provided company_id without an explicit company-access check in export_preview/export_file. That is a real data-scope risk.

Also, reprocessing clears/replaces line items idempotently, but it does not clear prior journal vouchers. Document detail and export currently read journal_vouchers[0], so a reprocessed document can still show/export stale mapping data.
These findings are blockers for the next deploy/proof round because they affect data isolation and correctness of real reviewed-document export.

allowed_scope: Fix the company-access check for the live export path
Add focused API/service tests for these exact cases
Small supporting refactors only if required to keep the patch clean and consistent
forbidden_scope: Do not reopen W5-12 architecture or redesign the line-item product flow
Do not turn this into COA glyph work, dashboard honesty work, or first-login work
Do not modify SIT runtime env or deploy flows; Copilot owns that lane
Do not broaden scope into product matching, OCR tuning, or Stage C timeout handling in this prompt

findings_to_close.symptom: The new live export path switches to backend data as soon as company_id is present, but export_preview/export_file do not explicitly enforce company access for that company.
Reprocessing creates a new journal voucher without clearing earlier ones, while document detail/export read the first voucher. A reprocessed document can therefore surface/export stale mapping data.

what_to_do: 1. Patch /v1/export/preview and /v1/export so the live export path cannot read another company's reviewed documents just by passing a foreign company_id. Reuse the repo's existing company-access pattern instead of inventing a new auth model.
2. Patch the reprocess path so document detail and export no longer read stale voucher data after a document is processed more than once.

3. Choose the most conservative repo-aligned fix for voucher correctness. Acceptable outcomes include either clearing/replacing old vouchers during reprocess or explicitly using the latest active voucher consistently in detail/export, as long as stale rows cannot leak into the real product path.
4. Add focused tests that would have caught both findings before review.
5. Keep the W5-12 line-item/export feature behavior intact; this prompt is a hardening pass, not a redesign.
implementation_guidance: For export access control, do not rely on the frontend to only send the selected company. Enforce access on the backend in the new live-export branch.
If you introduce a helper for export company resolution/access, keep it local and obvious rather than spreading new abstractions across unrelated modules.

For voucher correctness, think through all three surfaces together: persisted data on reprocess, GET /v1/documents/{id} detail payload, and build_export_records(). They must agree on which voucher is authoritative.
If the cleanest fix is voucher replace-on-reprocess, make sure tests cover that path and that journal lines are replaced coherently too.
If the cleanest fix is latest-voucher selection, make sure ordering is explicit and not left to ORM accident.
acceptance_criteria: A user without access to company B cannot preview or download company B's live export data by posting company_id=company_b.
A reprocessed document does not expose or export stale earlier voucher rows.
Document detail and export agree on the authoritative voucher after reprocess.
Focused API/service tests cover the new access-control path and the reprocess-voucher correctness path.
No regression to the core W5-12 behavior: line-item review/confirm/export still works for enable_stock=true companies, and header-only companies still work normally.
verification_expectation: Run focused pytest for export API/service and document workflow coverage.
Include exact test commands and results in the completion report.
If you change voucher persistence semantics, add or update the tightest possible test for reprocess behavior.
final_instruction_to_claude: Treat this as the last code-hardening pass before the next SIT redeploy/proof round for W5-12. Do not stop at analysis. Implement the patch, add the tests, push to dev, and write the completion report.
